subject.title: /new and /reset should support @agent targeting in multi-agent channels

question: What target-selection contract should Discord native `/new` and `/reset` use in multi-agent channels, and what should happen when no target is explicit?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but choosing between native `agent:` options, `@agent` mention parsing, a selector prompt, or fail-closed no-target behavior changes destructive command UX and security expectations.

options.title: Typed target selector
options.body: Add a native Discord `agent` selector or equivalent typed action and allow `/new` or `/reset` only when the target is explicit or the existing route is unambiguous.

options.title: Mention parsing
options.body: Accept `@agent` text in command arguments, which matches the issue wording but risks weaker validation and transport-specific parsing drift.

options.title: Defer broad multi-agent controls
options.body: Keep current routed-session behavior and leave explicit multi-agent destructive controls to a larger command-targeting design.

recommendation.title: Typed target selector
recommendation.body: Add a native Discord `agent` selector or equivalent typed action and allow `/new` or `/reset` only when the target is explicit or the existing route is unambiguous.

likelyOwner.reason: Their history anchors the shared native command session target helper that would likely need the product contract change.
